- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.50) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–4% per day.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., < 90% of mean), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- In high-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment > 0.75 for 3+ days), model often fails to capture momentum; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% in first 2–3 days of sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise in forecast tails.
